reply.summary:
I wrote 4 Playwright test files under acceptance/web-calculator/, with 55 tests that cover every acceptance criterion (AC-001 to AC-009, AC-011 to AC-024). Each test title starts with the criterion's ID and full wording. Results: all 55 pass against a reference page I built in /tmp from the plan, and all fail on an assertion or a missing element against the blank index.html. Both runs used --repeat-each 2. I deleted the blank index.html afterwards.

- **arithmetic.spec.mjs** covers AC-001, AC-002 (one test per digit 0–9), AC-003 to AC-009, AC-011, AC-012 and AC-023. The display is found by role "status" and buttons by role and exact name. The backspace button is matched by a name pattern (Backspace, Delete, DEL or ⌫). "Shows the value X" is checked with a pattern that requires the characters next to X not to be digits, decimal points or minus signs, as the spec defines. AC-023 checks there is no password field, login or sign-up control, or credential text, then runs a sum.
- **keyboard.spec.mjs** covers AC-013 to AC-017 and AC-024, each under 4 cases of "focus on the page document": focus on the body, on a digit button, on the = button and on the theme control. Focus is moved without a click or key press, so the page load still counts as fresh.
- **theme.spec.mjs** covers AC-018: the control is visible, the first activation gives light or dark, later activations alternate, and the body background colour differs between the two. It also covers AC-019 and AC-020: close the page, open a new one in the same browser profile, and the theme is kept. Each also has a variant where an earlier session saved the opposite theme.
- **layout.spec.mjs** covers AC-021 at 320×568: it requires `scrollWidth` to be 320. Scrollbars are hidden in this headless browser, so `scrollWidth` can't go below 320 and "at most 320" means exactly 320. Every button, the theme control and the display must also lie fully inside 0–320 px. AC-022 has 4 tests (light and dark, each for mouse hover and for focus by the Tab key) covering every button and the theme control.

Two checks on the reference page also failed when they should: a 340 px wide layout failed AC-021, and removing the hover styles failed the AC-022 hover tests.

Things that could affect the implementer:
- **Theme control name:** the theme control is found by a name matching theme, dark, light or mode, and may be a button, switch or checkbox.
- **Style transitions:** before reading styles, the AC-022 and AC-018 tests jump any running CSS transitions to their end state, so transitions can't make the tests flaky.
- **Other browsers:** the runner only uses Chromium, so AC-001 is checked from a file:// URL in Chromium, which is one of the browsers the criterion allows. Firefox is not tested.

reply.summary:
I wrote 11 Playwright files (.spec.mjs) under acceptance/web-calculator/. Every acceptance criterion has at least one test. The full suite passed against a reference build kept outside the checkout. The official blank-page run was only finished for 8 of the 11 files.

**Results**
- Reference build: all 68 tests pass, including the theme and interaction-state files repeated 3 times.
- Quick checks against deliberately broken copies of that build: the right tests failed for no focus style, no saved theme, a page wider than 320 px, and a missing preventDefault. A page taller than the viewport correctly passes.
- Official command on the blank index.html: 8 files fail the way they should, every failure on an assertion or on a locator action that finds no element, never on navigation or an error in the test code. These are arithmetic, theme, layout, interaction-states and keyboard AC-013/014/015/016.
- Not finished on the blank page: buttons-and-entry, keyboard-ac-017-escape and keyboard-ac-024-subtract. I started two runs in parallel and a run was killed at the time limit. Its Chromium processes became zombies that the container's PID 1 (a `sleep`) never cleans up. 473 of them used up the process limit, and Chromium can no longer start (spawn EAGAIN). These three files pass on the reference build, start with the required line, pass `node --check`, and are built the same way as the files that did fail correctly. Their real blank-page behaviour should still be confirmed in the system's own run.
- I created the blank index.html for these runs and deleted it again; only acceptance/web-calculator/ is changed.

**What the files cover**
- **buttons-and-entry:** AC-001, AC-002 (one test per digit 0–9), AC-003, AC-004 and AC-023 (no password, login or sign-up prompt, plus a sum that works).
- **arithmetic:** AC-005 to AC-009, AC-011 and AC-012. "Shows the value X" is checked with a regex: no digit, `.` or minus sign right before or after X.
- **keyboard-ac-013/014/015/016/017/024:** each keyboard criterion runs once for every case of "focus on the page document": the document body, and focus on button 0, +, =, C and the theme control.
- **theme:** AC-018 by mouse click and by the Space key. AC-019 and AC-020 each from a fresh profile and after the other theme was saved: the page is closed, a new page is opened in the same browser context, and data-theme is checked before any interaction.
- **layout:** AC-021 at 320×568. It checks scrollWidth is 320. Headless Chromium shows no scrollbar, so at most 320 means exactly 320. It then checks that every button, the display and the theme control lie fully inside the viewport after scrolling them into view vertically.
- **interaction-states:** AC-022 for all 19 buttons plus the theme control, in light and dark. Hover state, and focus reached by actually pressing Tab.

**Choices that affect the implementer**
- The display is found by role `status`. Buttons are found by exact accessible name (`+`, `-`, `×`, `÷`, `.`, `=`, `C`, digits). The backspace button by a name matching backspace, delete or ⌫. The theme control by a name matching theme, dark, light or mode, or by `#theme-toggle`.
- The body background (AC-018) and the AC-022 styles are read only after running CSS transitions are finished in the page. Without this, a transition caused a false failure.

No acceptance criterion was left without a test.

reply.summary:
I wrote Playwright acceptance tests under acceptance/web-calculator/ that cover every criterion from AC-001 to AC-024. Each test is titled with its criterion ID and the criterion's words; some titles add a short condition at the end, such as "(light theme)".

Files:
- **arithmetic.spec.mjs** covers AC-001 to AC-009, AC-011, AC-012 and AC-023. It clicks buttons found by role and name. "Shows the value X" is checked with a pattern that requires the characters around X not to be digits, decimal points or minus signs. AC-002 loops over every digit from 0 to 9, reloading the page each time. AC-011 records the display text at page load and compares it exactly after C. AC-023 also checks that there is no password field and no login, sign-up or credential text.
- **keyboard.spec.mjs** covers AC-013 to AC-017 and AC-024. Each criterion runs three times, once for each meaning of "focus on the page document": focus on the body, on a calculator button, and on the theme control.
- **theme.spec.mjs** covers AC-018 to AC-020. AC-018 checks that the attribute alternates over several activations and that the body background colour differs between the themes. AC-019 and AC-020 close the page and open a new one in the same browser context. One AC-020 test first saves dark, then switches to light, then reopens.
- **layout.spec.mjs** covers AC-021 and AC-022. AC-021 checks the page width at 320×568 and that the display, every button and the theme control lie fully within the 320 px width. AC-022 runs once per theme and checks each button and the theme control for a style change on hover and after Tab focus.

Test results against the blank index.html:
- **arithmetic, theme and layout:** every test failed on an assertion or a missing element, never on navigation or a script error (24, 8 and 6 failures across the two repeats).
- **keyboard.spec.mjs: not verified.** It has 36 tests over two repeats, so its run exceeded the 300-second limit and was killed before it produced a report. It uses the same patterns as the verified files and should fail the same way.

Caveats:
- The theme control is found as #theme-toggle, the id the plan chose, because the plan gives it no accessible name. The display is found by role "status", and the backspace button by a name matching backspace, delete or ⌫.
- AC-001 runs in Chromium only, because the system's test configuration uses Chromium. The Firefox part of that criterion is not exercised.

The temporary blank index.html has been deleted.

tests.title: AC-001 Opening index.html from the local filesystem as a file:// URL in a current Chromium-based or Firefox browser, with no server process running, displays the calculator, and clicking 1, 2, +, 3, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 15.

AC-002 For each digit d from 0 through 9, after a fresh page load, clicking the button labelled 1 and then the button labelled d results in the display area showing the value formed by the digit 1 followed by d.
AC-003 The page shows operator buttons labelled +, -, × and ÷, a decimal point button labelled ., an equals button labelled =, a clear button labelled C, and a backspace/delete button.
AC-004 After a fresh page load, clicking the buttons 1, 2 in sequence results in the display area showing the value 12.
AC-005 After a fresh page load, clicking 1, 2, +, 3, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 15.
AC-006 After a fresh page load, clicking 7, -, 1, 0, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value -3.
AC-007 After a fresh page load, clicking 6, ×, 7, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 42.
AC-008 After a fresh page load, clicking 8, ÷, 2, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 4.
AC-009 After a fresh page load, clicking 1, ., 5, +, 2, ., 2, 5, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 3.75.

AC-011 After a fresh page load, clicking 5, +, 3 and then C results in the display area showing exactly the same text it showed on the fresh page load, and then clicking 2, +, 2, = results in the display area showing the value 4.
AC-012 After a fresh page load, clicking 1, 2, 3 and then the backspace/delete button results in the display area showing the value 12 and its text not containing 123.
AC-023 Loading index.html shows the calculator without any login, sign-up or credential prompt, and every criterion above passes without the user entering any credential.
AC-013 After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 9, *, 3, Enter in sequence results in the display area showing the value 27. (focus on the document body)
AC-014 After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 2, +, 3, Enter in sequence results in the display area showing the value 5. (focus on the document body)
AC-015 After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 8, /, 4, Enter in sequence results in the display area showing the value 2. (focus on the document body)

AC-016 After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 4, ., 5 and then Backspace results in the display area text containing 4. and not containing 4.5. (focus on the document body)

AC-017 After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 5, +, 3 and then Escape results in the display area showing exactly the same text it showed on the fresh page load. (focus on the document body)
AC-024 After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 9, -, 4, Enter in sequence results in the display area showing the value 5. (focus on the document body)
AC-013 After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 9, *, 3, Enter in sequence results in the display area showing the value 27. (focus on a calculator button)

reply.summary: I wrote three Playwright test files under acceptance/web-calculator/: calculator.spec.mjs, theme.spec.mjs and layout.spec.mjs. They use .mjs because the runner rejects top-level await in .js files. There is a test for every AC ID from AC-001 to AC-024 (AC-010 does not exist in the spec). Each test title starts with the criterion ID and its words. AC-022 has four tests, covering hover and Tab focus in both the light and dark themes. I ran all three files against a throwaway calculator I wrote at index.html and every test passed, including with --repeat-each 2 on theme and layout. The calculator.spec.mjs run was a single pass, not a repeat. I did not run any test against the blank index.html, so I haven't confirmed they fail on assertions or locator actions there. The throwaway index.html is deleted, so the checkout has only the test files. Some tests rely on plan details: the display is found by role "status", and the theme control by a button name matching /theme/i. The AC-021 horizontal bounds check uses `toBeInViewport({ratio: 1})` after scrolling each element into view, plus `scrollWidth` equal to 320. This relies on headless Chromium hiding scrollbars.

tests.title: AC-001 Opening index.html from the local filesystem as a file:// URL with no server displays the calculator, and clicking 1, 2, +, 3, = results in the display area showing the value 15
AC-002 For each digit d from 0 through 9, after a fresh page load, clicking 1 and then d results in the display area showing the value formed by 1 followed by d
AC-003 The page shows operator buttons labelled +, -, × and ÷, a decimal point button labelled ., an equals button labelled =, a clear button labelled C, and a backspace/delete button
AC-004 After a fresh page load, clicking the buttons 1, 2 in sequence results in the display area showing the value 12
AC-005 After a fresh page load, clicking 1, 2, +, 3, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 15
AC-006 After a fresh page load, clicking 7, -, 1, 0, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value -3
AC-007 After a fresh page load, clicking 6, ×, 7, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 42
AC-008 After a fresh page load, clicking 8, ÷, 2, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 4
AC-009 After a fresh page load, clicking 1, ., 5, +, 2, ., 2, 5, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 3.75

AC-011 After a fresh page load, clicking 5, +, 3 and then C results in the display area showing exactly the same text it showed on the fresh page load, and then clicking 2, +, 2, = results in the display area showing the value 4
AC-012 After a fresh page load, clicking 1, 2, 3 and then the backspace/delete button results in the display area showing the value 12 and its text not containing 123
AC-013 After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 9, *, 3, Enter in sequence results in the display area showing the value 27

tests.title: AC-001 Opening index.html from the local filesystem as a file:// URL with no server displays the calculator, and clicking 1, 2, +, 3, = results in the display area showing the value 15
AC-002 For each digit d from 0 through 9, after a fresh page load, clicking 1 and then d results in the display area showing the value formed by 1 followed by d
AC-003 The page shows operator buttons labelled +, -, × and ÷, a decimal point button labelled ., an equals button labelled =, a clear button labelled C, and a backspace/delete button
AC-004 After a fresh page load, clicking the buttons 1, 2 in sequence results in the display area showing the value 12
AC-005 After a fresh page load, clicking 1, 2, +, 3, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 15
AC-006 After a fresh page load, clicking 7, -, 1, 0, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value -3
AC-007 After a fresh page load, clicking 6, ×, 7, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 42
AC-008 After a fresh page load, clicking 8, ÷, 2, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 4
AC-009 After a fresh page load, clicking 1, ., 5, +, 2, ., 2, 5, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 3.75

AC-011 After a fresh page load, clicking 5, +, 3 and then C results in the display area showing exactly the same text it showed on the fresh page load, and then clicking 2, +, 2, = results in the display area showing the value 4
AC-012 After a fresh page load, clicking 1, 2, 3 and then the backspace/delete button results in the display area showing the value 12 and its text not containing 123
AC-013 After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 9, *, 3, Enter in sequence results in the display area showing the value 27
AC-014 After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 2, +, 3, Enter in sequence results in the display area showing the value 5
AC-015 After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 8, /, 4, Enter in sequence results in the display area showing the value 2
AC-016 After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 4, ., 5 and then Backspace results in the display area text containing 4. and not containing 4.5

AC-017 After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 5, +, 3 and then Escape results in the display area showing exactly the same text it showed on the fresh page load
AC-023 Loading index.html shows the calculator without any login, sign-up or credential prompt, and every criterion above passes without the user entering any credential
AC-024 After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 9, -, 4, Enter in sequence results in the display area showing the value 5

reply.summary:
Wrote four Playwright files under acceptance/web-calculator/: calculator.spec.mjs, keyboard.spec.mjs, theme.spec.mjs and layout.spec.mjs. They cover AC-001 to AC-009 and AC-011 to AC-024; the spec has no AC-010. I used .mjs because the mandatory first line uses top-level await. I checked the tests with the system's command in two ways, then deleted the temporary index.html and src/. Against a throwaway implementation that followed the plan, all 94 test runs passed with --repeat-each 2. Against the blank index.html, all 47 tests failed, each on a locator action or an assertion; none failed on navigation or an error in my own code.

Choices to know about:
- AC-002 has one test per digit, with "(d=N)" appended after the criterion's words.
- The keyboard criteria (AC-013 to AC-017, AC-024) each run with focus on the document body, on the theme control and on the "1" button, because the "with focus on the page document" convention allows focus on any calculator element.
- AC-019 and AC-020 close the page and open a new page in the same context.
- AC-021 checks scrollWidth as exactly 320, because toHaveJSProperty has no "at most" form. It also requires each button, the display and the theme control to be fully in the viewport after scrolling to it.
- AC-022 is split into a hover test and a Tab-focus test for each theme. It records the default values of all six properties, finds the first one that changes, and asserts that property differs.
- The tests use #theme-toggle for the theme control and expect exactly 19 buttons, as the plan says.

reply.summary: I wrote four Playwright files under acceptance/web-calculator/ covering every criterion except AC-010, which the specification does not define. digits.spec.mjs covers AC-002 (one test per digit 0-9) and AC-004. operations.spec.mjs covers AC-001, 003, 005-009, 011-017 and 024, with clicks and keyboard keys. theme.spec.mjs covers AC-018, 019 and 020. layout.spec.mjs covers AC-021, AC-022 (one test each for the light and dark themes) and AC-023. I ran the suite twice with --repeat-each 2. First I used a throwaway implementation that I wrote to match the plan, and every test passed (22, 30, and 6 or 8 in the other two files). Then I used the blank index.html, and the theme and layout tests failed on a missing-element locator or on an assertion. I did not run the digits and operations files against the blank page. I deleted the temporary index.html and src/ afterwards.
